sources.text:
Ånderdalen National Park (Norwegian: Ånderdalen nasjonalpark) is located on the large island of Senja in Troms county, Norway.  The 134-square-kilometre (52 sq mi) park lies within Senja Municipality. The park was established by royal decree on 6 February 1970 and it was enlarged in 2004. The national park preserves this Northern Norwegian coastal landscape. The bedrock consists of hard granite rocks and the landscape image gives exciting impressions of the glacial forces that have worked on Senja. The coastal pine forest in Ånderdalen has in some areas primeval forest with over 600 years old trees and countless marble pines and lower. Along the river there are many lush hawked birch forests and floodplain forests.

The national park had no moose before 1940, but it now has a permanent population. It is also an important calving and grazing area for semi-domesticated reindeer. The most common smaller animals are red foxes, stoats, hares, small rodents, and two species of shrews. Seals occur at the heads of the fjords and otters are often seen along rivers. Trout and char are common, and salmon run right up the river to the lake Åndervatn.

stops.name: Ånderdalen National Park
stops.detail: Ånderdalen National Park liegt auf der großen Insel Senja im Kreis Troms, Norwegen. Der 134 Quadratkilometer große Park liegt in der Gemeinde Senja. Der Park wurde am 6. Februar 1970 durch königliches Dekret gegründet und in [datierter Quelle] erweitert. Der Nationalpark bewahrt diese nordnorwegische Küstenlandschaft. Der Grundstein besteht aus hartem Granitfelsen und das Landschaftsbild vermittelt spannende Eindrücke von den Gletscherkräften, die auf Senja gewirkt haben. Der Küstenkieferwald in Ånderdalen hat in einigen Gebieten Urwald mit über 600 Jahre alten Bäumen und unzähligen Marmorkiefern und darunter. Entlang des Flusses gibt es viele üppige Falkenbirkenwälder und Auenwälder.
